effect.purpose: Read-only Effect v4 source pinned to the tag matching the installed effect release — the authority on what v4 actually exports, plus the v3→v4 migration notes.

effected.purpose: Read-only source for @effected/github-actions, @effected/github and @effected/jsonc — the libraries this action is built on. Pin tracks the installed @effected/github-actions version.

orientation.layout: pnpm monorepo, one directory per published package under packages/<name>/ with src/, test files co-located, and its own CLAUDE.md. The sparse checkout materializes only github-actions, github, jsonc and schemastore in full; every OTHER packages/<name>/ directory exists but holds nothing but a README.md (the non-cone `README.md` pattern matches at any depth) — an empty-looking package is out of the sparse set, not missing upstream. This repo carries nine submodules of its OWN (.repos/cmark-gfm, commonmark-js, commonmark-spec, effect, mdast, mdast-util-from-markdown, mdast-util-mdx-expression, mdast-util-mdx-jsx, mdast-util-mdxjs-esm) — leave every one uninitialized. `sparse` cannot evict a nested submodule's worktree, because it belongs to a different repository, so a recursive init materializes .repos/effected/.repos/effect as a SECOND Effect clone that drifts off the top-level .repos/effect pin; an agent reading Effect source through this tree then gets a version nobody pinned, and effected stays permanently dirty. Repair with `savvy repos restore effected`, which deinitializes them. Verify with `git -C .repos/effected submodule status` — every line must start with `-`.
orientation.startHere: packages/<name>/src/index.ts for a package's real export surface, and its CLAUDE.md for the intended usage. Pinned to the release tag named by `ref`, so the checkout matches the published version this repo installs — re-pin whenever that version moves. A tag is a monorepo-wide release commit, so github-actions@X and app@Y from the same wave resolve to one commit. node_modules still wins on any disagreement.

notes.note: A fetch with `--recurse-submodules` (= yes) prints nine `Could not access submodule '.repos/<name>'` warnings and `Errors during submodule fetch: .repos/effected`, exit 1. This is EXPECTED and harmless — git descends into effected and warns for each of its nine nested gitlinks precisely because they are uninitialized, which is the state we want. Re-reproduced on git 2.56.0 at this pin: the fetch of origin and of both vendored submodules succeeds and nothing is left dirty. Do NOT try to fix it in this repo: verified against git 2.54.0 that `fetch.recurseSubmodules=false` and `submodule..repos/effected.fetchRecurseSubmodules=false` are both overridden by the explicit command-line flag, and adding `.gitmodules` to this entry's `sparse` changes nothing. `submodule..repos/effected.active=false` would silence it but makes `git submodule status` read uninitialized and every drift report claim missingWorktree — off-limits. `git fetch origin` and `--recurse-submodules=on-demand` are both silent, so the fix belongs in whatever client passes the flag (GitKraken's fetch-submodules setting). Separately: orphaned nested gitdirs can accumulate at `.git/modules/.repos/effected/modules/.repos/*` from some earlier recursive init — unversioned local metadata, safe to `rm -rf`, and NOT the cause of the warnings.

The okf bundle cites this repo by LINE ANCHOR. Re-verified at this pin (`acfd885`, the 0.31.0 -> 0.32.0 re-pin, Effect 4.1; only the `GitCommit.ts` anchors moved): `packages/github/src/GitBranch.ts:47-64` is the `@remarks` block on `upsert` (line 64 ends `on the bare target head.`, `readonly upsert` at 66); `okf/conventions/branch-on-github-error-kind.md` footnotes `GitHubError.ts:98,148,154,163,169`, `GitBranch.ts:42,219,222` and `PullRequest.ts:274-277` (`setAutoMerge`); `okf/invariants/commit-calls-carry-no-identity.md` footnotes `GitCommit.ts:88-139` (`GitCommitShape`) and `GitCommit.ts:97-101` (`createCommit`'s options). Verify with `grep -nF '<cited line text>' <file>`, never by eyeballing a `sed -n 'A,Bp'` range. Re-check every one on any re-pin. Separately, `git describe --tags` here reports a sibling package's tag, not this pin's; check the gitlink (`acfd885`) via repos_inspect instead.
